title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
prompt:
Return the values of a binary tree level by level, left to right, as an array of arrays.

Think of a district org chart: level 0 is the district, level 1 its schools, level 2 their classes. A report that lists "everyone at each level" is exactly this.

Write levelOrder(root). Helpers TreeNode, fromArray, toArray are at the top; keep them.

  • levelOrder(fromArray([3, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7])) returns [[3], [9, 20], [15, 7]]
  • levelOrder(fromArray([1])) returns [[1]]
  • levelOrder(null) returns []

Constraints: 0 to 2,000 nodes. Target: O(n).

tests.name: gaps: left to right order within a level

hints: Trigger: "level by level", "minimum depth", "nearest", "row by row" = BFS with a queue, not DFS.
Keep a queue holding exactly one level. Each round: read all those nodes' values into one array, and collect their children into the next level's queue. Stop when the queue is empty.

Shape:

let queue = [root];
while (queue.length > 0) {
  const values = [], nextQueue = [];
  for (const node of queue) {
    values.push(node.val);
    if (node.left) nextQueue.push(node.left);
    if (node.right) nextQueue.push(node.right);
  }
  levels.push(values);
  queue = nextQueue;
}
explain:
Time O(n): each node enters the queue once. Space O(w) where w is the widest level (up to about n/2 for a full tree). Swapping in a fresh array per level avoids queue.shift(), which is O(n) per call on a JS array.

Say it: "Level by level means BFS. I keep one level in a queue, read its values, and build the next level from the children. O(n) time, O(width) space."
